title.narrative: FAO - Stöd till institutionalisering och uppskalning av KIAMIS
FAO - Support to Institutionalization and Scale-up of KIAMIS

description.narrative:
Impact level Objective: A well coordinated data and information management system and evidence-based decision-making in the agriculture sector
Outcome level Objective: The Kenya Integrated Agriculture Management Information System is scaled nationally. FAO will achieve this provision of a government-owned system that strengthens coordination of the digital ecosystem in agriculture, and enhances policy and management decisions that are based on real-time data and information.
Specific Objectives are: to roll out the farmer registration and e-subsidy management modules to all counties; develop additional modules of KIAMIS; build human and institutional capacities for the operationalization, uptake and use of the System; strengthen coordination mechanisms and the linkages (both vertical and horizontal) for the successful implementation of KIAMIS - including the recently launched Digital Transformation Committee and its sub-committees; and identify and address policy gaps that hinder acceleration of digitization in the agriculture sector.
Outputs: Output 1. KIAMIS modules enhanced. . Output 2. Digital Solutions for Agriculture (DSA) framework developed. Output 3: Increased capacity for uptake and use of KIAMIS. Output 4: KIAMIS is scaled-up nationally. Output 5: Digital agriculture innovation centers (DAIC) and call centers created.

Detta är ett projekt för att stärka nationella och länsstyrelsers kapacitet för effektiv jordbruksdata och kunskapshantering genom ett integrerat informationssystem för jordbruksledning - Kenya Integrated Agriculture Management Information System (KIAMIS).

This is a project on strengthening National and County Governments capacity for effective agriculture data and knowledge management through an integrated Agriculture Management Information System - The Kenya Integrated Agriculture Management Information System (KIAMIS).

Output 1: KIAMIS modules developed
During the reporting period, the e-voucher system was deployed and is actively supporting vaccination and fertilizer subsidy programmes. However, progress in the development of other core modules including transactional data, routine data, and extension services has been slower than anticipated. This raises concerns given the limited remaining implementation period, with project closure expected by the end of 2026 and no provision for a no-cost extension.
Output 2: Digital Solutions for Agriculture (DSA) framework developed
Through the development of Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development (MoALD) systems have been integrated with KIAMIS to support livestock vaccination, traceability, and EUDR mapping. However, progress in establishing partnerships with financial institutions and insurance providers intended to leverage anonymized farmer data for credit scoring models has been limited. This constrains the potential for broader utilization of KIAMIS data to support financial inclusion.
Output 3: Increased capacity for uptake and use of KIAMIS
KIAMIS has been formally handed over to the Government, including key components such as the farmer registration module, farmer database, and e-voucher system. While this represents a significant milestone, gaps remain in the development and handover of outstanding modules. In addition, access to KIAMIS data at county level remains limited, and private sector engagement has been insufficient, which constrains broader system uptake and utilization.
Output 4: KIAMIS scaled up nationally through county level rollout
To support institutionalization of KIAMIS, the Government has developed the Agriculture Data, Information and Digital Policy and the accompanying Digital Agriculture Information Bill (2026). Once enacted, this framework is expected to provide a legal basis for the system and enable access to national budgetary resources, thereby supporting long-term sustainability beyond Swedish funding.
Output 5: Digital Agriculture Innovation Centres (DAIC) and Call Centres
Progress under this output has been significantly delayed. The explanations provided by the partner have not sufficiently justified the continued delays, particularly in light of the limited remaining implementation period. Given that similar challenges have been noted in previous reporting cycles, the Embassy and the partner will discuss the feasibility of discontinuing this output.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
